original_question: Suppose that A is a nilpotent group of automorphisms of a finite soluble group G. Is the Fitting height of G bounded in terms of |A| and |CG(A)|? An affirmative answer is known when(|G|, |A|) = 1(J. G. Thompson, even for soluble A, with improved bounds in subsequent papers of H. Kurzweil, A. Turull, B. Hartley–I. M. Isaacs), when A is cyclic(see 19.43), or when CG(A) = 1(E. C. Dade). Note that for any non-nilpotent finite group A there are finite soluble groups G of unbounded Fitting height with CG(A) = 1(S. D. Bell–B. Hartley).
target_in_paper: Problem 21.66 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)": "Suppose that A is a nilpotent group of automorphisms of a finite soluble group G. Is the Fitting height of G bounded in terms of |A| and |C_G(A)|?"
correct_elements: Your draft matches Problem 21.66 essentially verbatim. It has the correct setting (finite soluble group G), the correct acting object (a nilpotent automorphism group A), the correct invariant (the Fitting height of G), and the correct control parameters (|A| and |C_G(A)|). It also reproduces the same contextual remarks listed in the paper: the positive coprime case, the cyclic special case via 19.43, Dade's fixed-point-free case C_G(A)=1, and the Bell-Hartley counterexamples showing that the nilpotency assumption on A matters.
missing_details: For a fully stand-alone formulation, A should be stated explicitly as a finite subgroup A ≤ Aut(G).
The notation C_G(A) should be defined explicitly as the fixed-point subgroup {g in G : g^a = g for every a in A}.
The phrase "bounded in terms of |A| and |C_G(A)|" should be formalized as the existence of a function f such that h(G) ≤ f(|A|, |C_G(A)|) for all such pairs (G, A).
If full self-containment is desired, h(G) should be identified as the Fitting height of G, i.e. the least length of a normal series of G with nilpotent factors.
The list of known cases and counterexamples is explanatory context from the paper, not part of the core formal problem statement.
refined_question: Does there exist a function f such that, for every finite soluble group G and every finite nilpotent subgroup A ≤ Aut(G), the Fitting height h(G) of G (that is, the least length of a normal series of G with nilpotent factors) satisfies h(G) ≤ f(|A|, |C_G(A)|), where C_G(A) = {g in G : g^a = g for all a in A}?
justification: The draft is targeting Problem 21.66 exactly: the wording and even the surrounding remarks agree with the official formulation in the paper almost word-for-word. The only nearby item that materially sharpens the context is Problem 19.43, which 21.66 cites as the cyclic special case; in the current edition that special case is recorded as solved. The paper does not state an equivalent reformulation of 21.66, so the sharpest stand-alone rewrite is the direct boundedness question, with the implicit quantifier and notation made explicit.
